claims.statement: For A = {x+i : x <= X}, |r_d| <= 1 for every admissible ideal and this is sharp, so sum_{N(d)<=D}|r_d| ~ D and Type I holds exactly for D = o(X) = o(Q^{1/2}).
The number of admissible Gaussian ideals of norm <= D is ~ (3/2pi) D, the residue of zeta(s)L(s,chi_4)/zeta(2s) at s=1.
d divides x+i if and only if x == r_d (mod N(d)) for a single residue r_d with r_d^2+1 == 0.
For A = {x+i}, the bilinear incidence graph contains no 4-cycle, so G(n1,n2) = #{m : mn1, mn2 in A} <= 1 for n1 != n2. Holds from both sides, in m and in n alike.
Hypothesis (R1) of the asymptotic sieve for primes requires x^{2/3} < D(x) < x.
claims.citation: Friedlander-Iwaniec, Asymptotic sieve for primes, Ann. of Math. 148 (1998), p.1043 (arXiv:math/9811186)

claims.statement: 'for thin sequences A one cannot expect (R) to hold with D(x) > A(x)'.

x^{2/3} is the threshold below which the coefficient gamma(n,C) of hypothesis (B) is annihilated: 'd must be quite a bit smaller than N to ensure that mu(d) does not completely neutralize mu(n) ... our hypothesis (B) can be realistic only if D is somewhat larger than x^{2/3+eps}'.
The Friedlander-Iwaniec asymptotic sieve as stated cannot be applied to x^2+1: (R1) demands D > x^{2/3} while Type I caps at x^{1/2}, so the admissible range for D is empty.
Heath-Brown's density exponent alpha places the problems at alpha = 1 (Dirichlet), 3/4 (a^2+b^4), 2/3 (x^3+2y^3), and 1/2 (x^2+1).
claims.citation: Heath-Brown, Primes represented by x^3+2y^3, Acta Math. 186 (2001), p.2 of the Oxford ORA preprint

claims.statement: Heath-Brown did not use the asymptotic sieve: 'their condition (R1) is not quite met in our case ... Although it seems possible that Friedlander and Iwaniec's hypothesis (R1) might be relaxed sufficiently for our application, we have chosen instead to present our own version of the sieve argument.'
Heath-Brown's sequence has level of distribution X^{2-eps} for values of size X^3, i.e. x^{2/3-eps} -- short of (R1) by an epsilon.
For a^2+b^4 the level of distribution D = x^{3/4-5eps} is achieved, 'apart from the eps, the best that one can hope for'.
claims.citation: Friedlander-Iwaniec, X^2+Y^4 captures its primes, Prop. 3.5, p.962 (arXiv:math/9811185)

claims.statement: FI's Type I gain comes from applying the Davenport-Halberstam large sieve to the points nu/d with nu^2+1 == 0 (mod d), which for moduli in a short interval are spaced by 1/4D rather than 1/D^2.
claims.citation: X2Y4 Lemma 3.2 and surrounding text, p.957
claims.notes: This repo previously guessed the mechanism was Poisson summation in b. That was wrong; corrected in Note D.

claims.statement: FI prove the Type II bound B(x;N) << A(x)(log x)^{4-A} for x^{1/4+eta} < N < x^{1/2}(log x)^{-B}.
Over dyadic splits, max min(D_m, d_n) ~ sqrt(kappa) = |A|/Q^{1/2}. Measured ratio 0.85-0.92 across the family a^2+b^{2k}, k=2..6 (alpha 0.75 down to 0.583), and 1.26 for x^2+1 where sqrt(kappa)=1.
claims.notes: A degree heuristic supported across a one-parameter family, not a theorem. The C4-free lemma is the proved statement in the neighbourhood.

claims.statement: sum_m |sum_n mu(n) 1[mn in A]| ~ sqrt(MX) for M <= X, saturating at ~|A| for M >= X. Ratio to sqrt(MX) is 0.88-0.93, stable from X = 2e4 to 1e5.
In the window (B1) would require, M in (x^{1/2}, x^{3/4}), the measured bilinear sum shows no saving at all: S_mu/A(x) = 0.93, 1.00, 1.01.

Inside FI's proved Prop. 4.1 window the harness sees a^2+b^4 drop to S_mu/|A| = 0.16-0.52 while x^2+1 sits at 0.84-1.01; outside it both saturate. Confirms direction, not magnitude: a log-power saving is invisible over one decade.

Every level-of-distribution result in this literature concerns primes or smooth numbers in arithmetic progressions, where A(x) = x^{1-o(1)}; the best exponent reached is 5/8-eps. x^{7/12-eps} is Maynard (2020), not Iwaniec, whose contribution is the well-factorability of the linear sieve weights.
claims.notes: Corrected: an earlier version of this claim attributed 7/12 to Iwaniec, and justified inadmissibility by 'weights cannot lift a counting bound', which over-reaches -- sparse-moduli and signed-weight estimates evade counting bounds. The sound reason is that ASP's (R) sums absolute values over all squarefree d <= D.
claims.citation: Maynard arXiv:2006.07088 pp.2-3 (BFI 4/7; Maynard 7/12); Pascadi (Lichtman 66/107, Pascadi 5/8); Polymath 8a arXiv:1402.0811 (Zhang 1/2+1/584, Polymath 1/2+7/300)

claims.statement: Iwaniec (1978) proved that irreducible an^2+bn+c with a>0 and c odd takes P_2 values infinitely often, via a lower-bound weighted sieve; this remains the record for x^2+1.
claims.notes: The original is paywalled; statement taken from an MSc exposition (arXiv:1910.02885), so it is second-hand and classed accordingly.

claims.statement: FI's Type I gain for a^2+b^4 comes from Poisson summation in the b variable.
claims.notes: Guessed by this repo, then refuted by reading X2Y4 p.957: the mechanism is a Davenport-Halberstam large sieve over the roots nu of nu^2+1 == 0 (mod d). Kept so it is not silently re-asserted.

claims.statement: The obstruction for x^2+1 is Type I, not Type II, so the bilinear programme is the wrong half.
claims.notes: Asserted in this repo, then withdrawn. ASP p.1045 shows (R1) is precisely the condition that hypothesis (B) is non-vacuous, so the two are one hypothesis and the dichotomy was malformed.

claims.statement: The Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec sieve (Ann. of Math. 141 (1995), sec.6), as used by Green-Sawhney, needs Type I only at level X^{1/2}(log X)^{-C} and Type II with arbitrary 1-bounded coefficients over N(b) in [(log X)^C, X^{3/8}].
claims.notes: Read at two removes: a subagent's report of Green-Sawhney Lemma 3.2, which itself quotes DFI. Neither DFI nor Green-Sawhney has been read directly in this repo. Reading DFI sec.6 is the top open task.

claims.statement: x^2+1 meets DFI's Type I hypothesis: Note B gives sum_{d<=D}|r_d| ~ D, so at D = X(log X)^{-C} the error is A(x)(log X)^{-C}.
claims.notes: Depends on dfi-typeI-budget, which is itself second-hand. The arithmetic is this repo's own and is sound; the requirement it is matched against is not verified at source.

claims.statement: x^2+1 fails DFI's arbitrary-coefficient Type II hypothesis outright: worst-case theta = 1.000, 0.999, 0.999 across N(m) in [10,100), [100,1000), [1000,1682) at X = 2e4. With beta = mu the same ranges give 0.627, 0.775, 0.825.

Green-Sawhney prove an asymptotic for primes p^2+nq^2 with p,q prime, n = 0 or 4 mod 6; at n=4 this settles Friedlander-Iwaniec's Gaussian Primes Conjecture. Their sequence has alpha = 1 and is not thin by FI's own criterion.
claims.citation: Green-Sawhney, Primes of the form p^2+nq^2, arXiv:2410.04189v3 Theorem 1.1 p.1 and p.2; FI Conjecture 1.1, arXiv:1811.05507v1 p.3

claims.statement: Two sieves break parity below x^{2/3}: Xiannan Li unconditionally, to exponential density 2/3 - gamma/3 for gamma < 5/67 (approx x^{0.6418}), and Merikoski conditionally on exceptional characters at 5/8. Neither reaches x^{1/2}.
claims.citation: Li, as reported with Maynard ICM survey Question 21; Merikoski arXiv:2108.01355
claims.notes: Quoted via subagent extraction with verbatim checks by an adversarial reviewer; the papers were not read in this repo.

claims.statement: Ford-Maynard Theorem 4.16 gives C^-(gamma,theta,nu) = 0 whenever gamma < 1/2 and gamma not in [theta,theta+nu]; Theorem 2.4 gives C^-(P_eps) = 0 at gamma = 1/2 with eps losses, remarking that 'one cannot hope to obtain non-trivial lower bounds on primes without some additional assumptions'. The escape named is divisor-bounded weights. x^2+1 sits at gamma = 1/2 exactly.
claims.citation: Ford-Maynard, On the theory of prime producing sieves, arXiv:2407.14368, Thm 2.4 p.6 and Thm 4.16 p.17

claims.statement: Merikoski proves infinitude of primes a^2+b^2 with b in B for |B cap [0,Y]| >> Y^{1-delta}, without using ASP. His A(X) ~ X^{1/2}|B| = X^{1-delta}, so alpha ~ 1-delta; his large sieve needs N << X^{-eta}|B|, so |B| = 1 empties the Type II range at any delta.
claims.citation: Merikoski, On Gaussian primes in sparse sets, arXiv:2302.11331v3, Thms 1.1-1.3; Compositio Math. 161 (2025), 181-243

claims.statement: Ford-Maynard (arXiv:2407.14368) restates or relaxes FI's hypothesis (R1).
claims.notes: Conjectured by this repo as 'the likeliest place for a restated or relaxed (R1)'. Refuted: the paper never cites ASP, never states (R1) or (B1)-(B3), and never mentions gamma(n,C).

claims.statement: No sector equidistribution result, however narrow, bears on the line Im z = 1, because sectors are two-dimensional and the line is not.
claims.notes: Asserted in Note A, then refuted: a sector anchored at arg = 0 is a horizontal strip, and Harman-Lewis harvest exactly that to get primes m^2+n^2 with n < p^0.119. The line is the width ~X^{-1/2} limit of the family, and an asymptotic there would prove Landau's fourth problem.

claims.statement: The line Im z = 1 is the width ~X^{-1/2} limit of the narrow-sector family. Unconditional asymptotics reach width X^{-3/10+eps} (Ricci), GRH reaches X^{-1/2+eps} for individual sectors, and Harman-Lewis get a lower bound at width X^{-0.381}.
claims.notes: Ricci's thesis (Univ. Michigan 1976) is unpublished; the X^{-3/10+eps} figure is second-hand from three agreeing restatements.

claims.statement: For fixed m, {n : mn in A} is the arithmetic progression n_0 + Z*conj(m), because Im(mn)=1 is a line whose homogeneous solutions are n = t*conj(m).
mu of the Gaussian ideal (x+i) equals mu(x^2+1) as an integer, since each rational prime dividing x^2+1 contributes exactly one prime ideal with the same exponent.

Up to the non-squarefree correction, the Type II sum equals sum_q |sum_{x<=X, x==r_q mod q} mu(x^2+1)| -- a Bombieri-Vinogradov statement for mu(x^2+1) in arithmetic progressions, at moduli up to X^{3/4} for a sequence of X terms.
claims.notes: The X^{3/4} range comes from DFI's Type II window, which this repo knows at two removes; if that window differs, the level changes.

claims.statement: The per-progression saving rho = S/(pairs*sqrt(X/M)) is flat in X: fitted rho ~ (log X)^c gives c = -0.026 and +0.039 in the two best-sampled bands (8348 and 68784 pairs) over X = 1e4..1e7. So the law is sqrt(MX) with no log-power correction.
claims.notes: Prime moduli only; the all-moduli cross-check at scale is not yet run. The constant rho ~ 0.655 is 0.87 of the random-walk prediction 0.755 and is unexplained.
